Definition: a trip (of the foot); figuratively, an infliction (of disease)
BiblicalUsage: Blood on the doorposts keeps the plague from destroying Israel, and the LORD Himself becomes a stone of stumbling to the houses that reject Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the same LORD is both shelter and stumbling: the blood keeps the plague away, and the stone trips the proud, and which He is to me depends on whether I trust Him or trip over Him.
